text:
oncall-bot: 🚨 Pager: Continuous-batch perf cliff detected (cluster=jetstream-3, shard=7). Alert: queue_latency_p99 > 2s and kvcache_evictions/sec spike.
ash_k: seeing it on dashboards, tailing logs now.
maria_g: moving to triage. any customer impact yet?
leo_s: logs show rapid KV evictions and microbatch sizes dropping to 1 repeatedly. suspect prefetch loop.
ash_k: starting targeted scrape on jetstream-3. grabbing /metrics and /proc stats.
jessica_p: I can take customer comms if it's a user-facing regression. who owns the affected routes?
sam_r: looks like requests to the hosted/chat API routed to model-rank-2 are returning 504s at scale, some customers seeing increased latency. CS ticket #C-2298 created by cs-bot.
ash_k: copying relevant log snippet:
```
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z WARN kvcache/evict.go:142 eviction burst: 1246 items/sec
2026-03-17T09:12:03Z INFO batch/queue.go:87 microbatch size=1 latency=2100ms pending=420
2026-03-17T09:12:04Z ERROR serve/worker.go:233 kv-miss-rate=0.72
```
maria_g: thanks. hypothesis: a recent autoscaler change reduced prefetch window, combined with a burst of high-concurrency short queries causes constant KV churn and prevents batching.
leo_s: can we roll a config tweak to increase prefetch_count and raise continuous_batch_min_microbatch to 8?
ash_k: recommend a two-step mitigation: 1) emergency policy: throttle incoming concurrency from 100 -> 60 on jetstream-3 via nginx weight, 2) patch runtime flags: prefetch_window=64, min_microbatch=8, disable_kv_eviction_adaptive=true.
jessica_p: I'll draft customer status: "We're investigating increased latency for chat routes; mitigation in progress."
sam_r: I'll queue the nginx throttle now. command: `infractl route-weight --cluster jetstream-3 --weight 60 --routes /v1/chat`
sam_r: throttle applied, verified by route metrics, QPS down ~40%. pending backlog is decreasing.
leo_s: starting runtime flag rollout to canary node set (shard 7a). patch command:
```
kubectl -n infra set env deployment/serve-runtime PREFETCH_WINDOW=64 MIN_MICROBATCH=8 DISABLE_KV_ADAPTIVE=true
```
ash_k: logs from canary show eviction rate dropping to ~80/sec and microbatch size rising to 6-9. latency p99 down to 700ms.
maria_g: good. roll to remaining nodes with 15s stagger. watch for regressions.
sam_r: rolling to remaining nodes in shards 7 and 8 now.
cs-bot: CS ticket C-2298 updated: "Mitigation in progress; partial relief observed. On-call escalated."
jessica_p: sent initial customer update. will update again after full rollout.
leo_s: small follow-up: we should also revert the prefetch autoscaler commit from last night in staging — it reduced long-window prefetching. open a PR to revert.
ash_k: created hotfix PR #5129 to patch defaults; marking urgent. link: https://git.internal/redwood/serve-runtime/pull/5129
maria_g: monitoring for 10m. once stable, we'll unwind nginx throttle slowly.
sam_r: backlog cleared and p99 stable ~600ms across cluster.
jessica_p: sending status update to affected customers: "Issue largely mitigated; working on root cause and permanent fix."
leo_s: postmortem notes to capture: race between autoscaler change + short-query workload, insufficient min_microbatch, no circuit-breaker on eviction spike.
ash_k: adding on-call follow-up tasks: increase test coverage for high-concurrency short-query scenarios, add emergency autoscaler kill switch, and add eviction spike alert with runbook.
maria_g: handing off to next oncall (ash_k -> leo_s) for overnight watch.
ash_k: acknowledged. good job team. :thumbsup:
__notes: This document is a synthesized Slack-thread-style incident coordination log. Messages are concise and reflect real-time on-call workflow: alert, hypothesis, mitigations (throttle + runtime flag), canary rollout, customer comms, and handoff.
